description: OpenClaw via npm global - the route that produces no .app and no Caskroom row.
demo_beat: step 4 coverage - the same agent, a different install shape
why: 50-autonomous covers the cask and asserts app>=1 and brew>=1. Neither fires here: an npm global installs no .app bundle and creates no Caskroom entry, so a fleet that standardised on the npm route would look completely clean to those two branches. app and brew are pinned to 0 deliberately - if either becomes non-zero this scenario has stopped testing what it was built to test. file>=1 was a correction: ~/.openclaw was predicted to appear only once the agent RUNS, but the npm install creates it immediately, which makes the state dir an install-time signal for this route and not merely a runtime one.
unexplained: Both this scenario and 20-cli-agents report the state dir under TWO users - /Users/admin/ and /Users/runner/ - though only admin ran anything, and 00-baseline shows neither. Most likely /Users/runner is aliased to admin's home in the Cirrus base image, which would mean one artifact is reported twice under two apparent users. If that is right it is a real dedup hazard for the collector, which keys findings per device and per user. NOT YET VERIFIED - do not build dedup logic on this until someone confirms it with KEEP_VM=1.
